key_insight: Reliable AI work requires more than a capable model: it requires a complete system connecting the model, execution infrastructure, and a persistent workspace. This paper proposes a unified, work-centric perspective on these agents.
problem_solved: Agent research lacks a shared framework for understanding how AI systems reliably complete delegated tasks across tools, applications, and workflows.
method: Treat work agents as integrated systems rather than standalone foundation models.
Examine how foundation models and runtime harnesses work together to execute delegated tasks.
Center task execution in stateful workspaces that retain context and changes across steps.
impact: This perspective encourages practitioners to design and assess the full agent system—not just its underlying model—when building AI for complex digital work. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific optimization techniques and empirical results cannot be summarized.
visual_elements: System diagram connecting foundation model, runtime harness, tools, and stateful workspace.
Workflow showing a delegated task progressing through multiple applications.
Side-by-side illustration contrasting information generation with digital work execution.
Workspace timeline showing how context and task state persist across actions.
paper_title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
paper_authors: Zishan Xu, Enjun Du, Mingqi Gao, Cheng Yang, Junhao Shen
